locations.description: A bolted-down table, four chairs, a fan that turns by hand. One chair keeps the red pencil. The papers on the table are the reason anyone descends the corridor at all.
Dosimeters in a row on a felt-lined tray beside a brass clock on a leather hinge. The clockmaker works here. Every figure has a drift, and the drift is normal.
A chalkboard in the children's corridor, numbers in children's chalk and adults' fingers, half-erased guesses and one date. The midwife writes in pencil so the truth can change its mind quietly.
The administrative center of the Dose Ledger institution, where dispute queues, appeal requests, and roster clearance checks converge before Dr. Vel's desk.
A narrow decontamination checkpoint with turnstiles, badge deposit slots, and survey meters where returning scavengers are triaged before entering clean bays.
Wind packs grey dust against the outer face of the blast doors where the apron dips toward the drainage run. The meter stirs the moment the hatch swings back.
A cupola of poured concrete with a viewing slit worn smooth by elbows. Its roof seams were caulked with sheet lead, and the caulking has begun to fail.
Runoff crosses the intake weir in a thin black line and leaves its sediment on the stones. The mud here holds its reading long after the water moves on.
Fallout settled into the leaf litter and stayed there. Understory growth comes back each spring a little wrong, and the meter climbs as the trail nears the treeline.
The collapsed wards shed their dust into the stairwells and catch basins below. Broken masonry holds the contamination the way a gutter holds rain.
Craters turned the hardstand into a bowl for settling fallout. Gravel ground to powder by tracked vehicles gives the dust a ride on every wind.
Black ice bridges the marsh with last season's sediment frozen mid-column. The crossing is slow, and slow is what the meter notices.
The ridge burned bare, and now the wind does the sorting, leaving what fell against its spine. There is nothing up there to hide behind.
Churned gravel and diesel soot mark where the garrison runs its checkpoint traffic. The readings are moderate, steady, and completely indifferent to whose flag is flying.
